recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No further core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-11055 unless CBCC later makes a new decision about the Consent provision model or the interaction between purpose-of-use tags and security labels.
issue_request: FHIR-11055 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Consent. The original request asked to remove DSTU2 Consent.except.purpose, but the final resolution instead approved adding the comment "When the purpose of use tag is on the data, access request purpose of use shall not conflict" to purpose and securityLabel.
initial_application: Historical commit 0f594b3938a50781639ecd7fa5930288595d9bfe, titled "Definition and comment changes for CR 11055 and CR 11056," applied the approved sentence in the old Consent spreadsheet source by replacing the purpose comment and appending the same sentence to the securityLabel comment. Later refactors carried the guidance into source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml as Consent.provision.purpose and Consent.provision.securityLabel.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current model represents the old Consent.except family as Consent.provision with recursive nested provisions. Related FHIR-11056 was applied by the same historical commit and already has an audit commit on the combined branch. Later FHIR-36354 refined the hierarchical-security-label portion of the securityLabel comment while preserving the FHIR-11055 purpose-of-use sentence.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The authoritative current StructureDefinition source already contains the approved purpose-of-use conflict sentence on Consent.provision.purpose and retains it in Consent.provision.securityLabel. Because the final Jira disposition did not require removing the purpose element, the continued presence of Consent.provision.purpose is correct.

related_jiras.note: Applied in the same historical commit and concerned the adjacent Consent.except/provision.securityLabel definition; already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published Consent issue refined hierarchical security-label wording in Consent.provision.securityLabel while preserving the FHIR-11055 sentence.
